newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH NEDCAR FAILS TO GET LICENCE FOR NIGHTSHIFTS.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH NEDCAR FAILS TO GET LICENCE FOR NIGHTSHIFTS.

text.p: Dutch carmaker Nedcar has failed to get a permit from the ministry of social affairs to introduce nightshifts, which could have boosted production hours by one quarter, company officials said on Thursday.
"We are looking for an alternative to lenghten our production hours, said Nedcar spokesman Fokko Haanstra, adding it was of vital importance to increase output.
Nedcar, a joint venture between Volvo Car , Mitsubishi Motors Corp and the Dutch government, aims to boost production to 280,000 cars in 1998 from a planned output of 145,000 in 1996.

In August Nedcar said it was failing to meet this year's output targets. Mitsubishi Motors Europe in August told Dutch media the company wanted to step up its production of vehicles in Europe and it might have to consider producing cars at alternative sites unless Nedcar raised output.

The ministry of social affairs said it would not give the permit to start a permanent nightshift in the Nedcar plant in the southern town of Born, as it would be in contradiction with the law to accept more than 28 nightshifts in 13 weeks.

Nedcar earlier this month applied for a licence to introduce nightshifts as it was of vital importance for the company to increase its production by a quarter to 5,000 hours annually to meet its output target.
